summary: Mostly no. On BTC, ETH and SOL, every session setting on 1h did the same as random candles. On 4h, so did the London, New York and Monday range breaks. The result that holds up is narrow: on 4h in uptrends, price crossing up through the previous day's high beat random entries by 0.7% after 20 candles, while in downtrends it was the same as random.

notes: On 1h, the default timeframe, every setting did the same as random entries. Price crossing down through the London session low gave 1,140 entries in 931 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.14% behind random, inside the luck band of -0.24% to 0.25%. Crossing up through the previous day's high landed 0.13% ahead, also inside a band of -0.18% to 0.18%.

The 4h cross up through the previous day's high shows why regimes matter. Pooled, it was 0.37% ahead of random, inside the band. In uptrends, its 728 entries in 371 moves beat random by 0.7%, and still did without their strongest stretch, between Dec 19, 2023 and Dec 22, 2023. The 503 downtrend entries were 0.03% behind random, the same as random. The uptrend gap showed at 20 and 100 candles but not at 10 or 50.

Holding above the previous day's high on 4h enters about four and a half times as often as the cross. It looked 0.51% better than random, but SOL's 68 entries between Aug 10, 2021 and Sep 9, 2021 carry the result. Without them, it was the same as random. On daily the same level had only 28 separate moves, under the 30 needed for a verdict.

The worse-than-random results also rest on single stretches. Buying as price crossed down through the London low on 4h was 0.74% behind random, just past the band's -0.72%. That rests on two entries between Apr 10, 2024 and Apr 12, 2024. In downtrends, holding above the London midpoint on 4h was 0.32% worse than random only because of signals on Nov 10–11, 2022, during the FTX collapse.

The Monday range did the same as random on every timeframe. On 4h in uptrends, the cross up through Monday's high beat random by 0.65%, but only because of entries between Dec 27, 2020 and Jan 2, 2021. The short on a cross down through Monday's low was the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily.

For a long DCA bot on 1h, session levels add no timing on these pairs, so you can leave them out and let the DCA orders and take profit do the work. On 4h, test the cross up through the previous day's high as a filter beside a 200-day SMA trend condition. Its gain did not show within 10 candles, so a tight take profit would not capture it. In downtrends it did nothing, so the filter only made a difference with the trend condition beside it.
